newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher across board.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher across board.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended sharply higher Friday, with gold jumping as the U.S. dollar slid, and platinum group metals soaring in the continued absence of Russia from the market.

"Fund shortcovering led the rally in gold and silver, after a break out from recent ranges, but the big fundamental change Friday was the huge fall in the U.S. dollar against the yen," Refco New York economist James Steel said.
"Meanwhile, the physical PGM market just got even tighter, with refiners struggling to borrow palladium in particular," he said.

COMEX June gold ended up $4.50 an ounce at $349.30, ahead of the expiry of COMEX June gold options Friday, and after climbing to the highest intraday level since April 14 at $349.50. Estimated total volume in COMEX gold was only a little above average though at 45,000 lots.

June gold's five-day moving average crossed above its 20-day moving average, for the first time since late February, suggesting the latest leg of the year-long downtrend may be over, technical analysts said.
But resistance was seen around $350.00, not far from the contract's 50-day moving average, analysts said.
COMEX June gold had been trapped in a $340-345 range for nearly a month, after sliding to contract lows at $339.50 on April 16.
But the range breakout Thursday led to some shortcovering by funds, and was reflected in a 2,600 lot fall in COMEX gold open interest Thursday to 164,348 contracts, analysts said.

"We've become less bearish, but the move up late in the day was only on thin volume ahead of the June gold option expiry," said Christ Foster, fund manager with Friedberg Mercantile Group, based in Toronto.
Spot gold ended quoted $347.80/30, after gold was fixed at $345.85 in London Friday afternoon, its highest level since April 14. In New York Thursday spot gold ended quoted around $343.50/00.

One factor behind the gold rally Friday was the huge slide in the U.S. dollar against the yen, to its lowest levels in three and a half months Friday, on fears of central bank intervention against the dollar.

Part of the reason for the fall in gold prices in the past year to four year lows has been the steady rise in the U.S. dollar, making gold more expensive in many currencies, but this may now be reversed, analysts said.

U.S. bond yields also fell early Friday after a speech by Federal Reserve chairman Greenspan Thursday night was interpreted to mean a further Fed monetary policy tightening may be deferred from May 20 until July.
Precious metals prices have tended to be inversely correlated with real interest rates recently.
Gold equities continued to lead gold prices higher Friday also, with the Philadelphia Stock Exchange's .XAU index of gold and silver stocks climbing to its highest level since March 27.
Silver was dragged higher by the rally in gold fRiday with COMEX July silver ending up 2.0 cents at $4.880, after seeing a session high at $4.925, its highest level since early April.
But platinum was relatively even stronger than gold, with the October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread climbing to a new high for the contracts at $35.40 an ounce.
NYMEX July platinum ended up $9.90 at $389.40 an ounce, after seeing a two month high intraday at $389.80, while the July/October contango narrowed sharply to just 20 cents.
Meanwhile, NYMEX June palladium was locked limit-up most of the day, ending up $6.00 an ounce at $163.90 an ounce, after setting a new contract high at $163.90.
In the physical market, palladium was fixed in London Friday at $164.50, its highest level since April 24, 1995.
Short term lease rates jumped for both platinum and palladium, with the one month implied rate for palladium climbing over 20 percent.

PGM dealers have been forced to borrow the metals to meet forward sales commitments, as Russian supplies have been disrupted since December, analysts said. Russia accounts for about 60 percent of world palladium supplies and about 25 percent of world platinum supplies.

PGM refiners and fabricators have also allowed inventories to run down, believing the metal will be available more cheaply once Russia returns to the market, but in the meantime hedge funds have been building long positions in both the physical and derivatives markets, pressuring shorts into covering some positions, analysts said.
((Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, 212-959-1640))
